b: In the book Gangsters of Capitalism by Jonathan M. Katz, the author writes that the British allegedly used chlorine gas against Chinese forces during the Boxer Rebellion. He cites a number of Chinese sources which claim that the British used a "chlorine gas cannon" in the vicinity of Beicang. One source is the journalist Li Boyuan who elaborates: "People only had to inhale the gas to die where they stood; they had no need to be in the vicinity of those cruel shells when they landed".
Is this just a misinterpretation of concussive force from artillery shells? And are there any Western sources that support the theory of it being poison gas?
